minutes.headline: Select Board appointed members to Planning Board and Housing Authority and ratified three town hires; TC Passios committee interviews held.
minutes.summary: The board held joint meetings to fill vacancies on the Planning Board and Housing Authority, granted a one-day beer and wine license, and interviewed four candidates for the TC Passios building design committee. It ratified a Council on Aging van driver, a recreation director and an assistant town manager/HR director. The town manager reported on grants, the 925 Mass Ave search warrant and the draft special town meeting warrant, including a non-binding question on demolishing the old primary school. A resident objected to the three-minute public comment rule.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the TC Passios building committee means the project is not a done deal and whether voters still decide; objected to the three-minute public comment rule applying only to the public and not to the board.

what_happened.line: The Select Board and Planning Board met jointly to nominate Marissa Thompson to a Planning Board vacancy; the minutes do not record an audible outcome.
The Select Board and Housing Authority voted jointly on a nomination of Ron Dion to the Housing Authority vacancy; the minutes do not record an audible outcome.
The board ratified three town hires: a Council on Aging van driver, a recreation director, and an assistant town manager/HR director.
The board interviewed four candidates for the TC Passios building design committee and set the remaining interviews for October 8, with the vote the following week.
The board reviewed the draft special town meeting warrant, including a non-binding question on demolishing the old primary school, and will settle liquor license article details October 8.

why_it_matters: The special town meeting warrant sets what voters will be asked to decide on November 12, including a land purchase, a liquor license article and a non-binding question on the old primary school.
The TC Passios design committee and the planned design RFP come before any request to voters to fund construction, so a cost estimate is expected before a funding vote.
Street light ownership and the old primary school demolition cost, as stated by a board member, bear on future town budgets, mostly taxes.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main appointments, the license, and the headline grant and land figures. Differences are mostly misheard names and garbled figures. The one real conflict is the Helen Godin vote, which the official minutes leave without an outcome. Our minutes also name the wrong board for the attendees: the official minutes show the Select Board members present, while ours list Planning Board people.
